calldata.note: Identical setAttribute call on two fresh registries, same identity/attr key/validity, differing only in the 128-byte value payload (all 0x00 vs all 0xff). Storage and log costs are identical, so the 1536-gas difference is pure calldata composition: the EVM charges 16 gas/non-zero byte vs 4 gas/zero byte, i.e. 12 gas/byte (= 16 - 4). This explains the small (+~12 gas) calldata artifacts observed elsewhere (e.g. the Sepolia dry-run) when signature/address byte patterns change the zero/non-zero byte count. Verified identical (12 gas/byte) at optimizer runs 1, 200 and 10000.

summary.finding: The ranking of standards by createIdentity gas is identical at all three optimizer settings (runs in {1,200,10000}). Every runtime message-call operation (all update ops, and the createIdentity of ERC-1056/ERC-721/CVIN-Combined/MOBI-VID-V2, which are ordinary calls) moves by <0.4% across settings. The single larger swing is ERC-725xy createIdentity (14.2%), which is a one-time contract DEPLOYMENT: higher optimizer runs deliberately produce larger deployed bytecode (optimizing runtime cost over deploy size), so deploy gas rises with runs. This is expected and does not change ERC-725xy's position as by far the most expensive to instantiate. The headline gas comparison is therefore robust to the solc optimizer setting; it is not an artifact of runs=200.

metadata.method: Per runs value: edit hardhat.config.js 0.8.24 optimizer.runs, hardhat clean && compile, then measure real receipt.gasUsed. Config restored to runs=200 and recompiled afterwards.
